bullets.title: Momentum factor down 23% in 10 days; de-grossing accelerates across semis/AI infra
bullets.body: MS QDS reports the MSZZMOMO momentum factor fell 23% from its June 23 peak — longs -12%, shorts +13% — in just 10 business days vs. a historical median of ~30. US L/S gross leverage is at a one-year low, and OPCO notes correlations are at their lowest since July 2024, when an 8.5% drawdown followed 12 days later. Levered ETFs are short gamma in Semis (-$1.7bn/1% SOX), NDX (-$2.8bn/1%), and AI single-names (-$1.3bn/1%), with SK Hynix ADR supply hitting this week as an additional overhang.

bullets.title: Chinese open-source AI models now >30% of US token usage; DeepSeek building own inference chip
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side desks flag that Chinese models (DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM) represent >30% of US company token usage since February — vs. an 11% 12-month average — and Chinese firms are shifting 46% of AI accelerator budgets to domestic chips vs. 30% today. DeepSeek is developing its own inference chip, and Zhipu AI is exploring custom ASICs. A potential US ban on Chinese models could benefit NVDA Nemotron and GOOGL, while a Chinese export restriction on advanced domestic models is also under MOFCOM/NDRC discussion.

bullets.title: AMZN raises $25B in bonds for AI capex — fourth debt raise YTD totaling ~$53B
bullets.body: Amazon is raising $25B from a bond sale earmarked for AI infrastructure, its fourth debt raise this year bringing the YTD total to roughly $53B. MS and Citi both flag hyperscaler capital raises as a signal of ongoing compute scarcity and demand for power infrastructure. This validates the 'time to power' thesis even as those stocks saw sharp weakness last week (WULF -19%, SEI -15%, VST -10%).

bullets.title: Jefferies and 22V warn on AI capex ROI risk; US 10Y >4.5% flagged as equity warning signal
bullets.body: Jefferies warns of growing investor risk around returns on debt-financed US AI capex, arguing hyperscaler share prices are the key confidence indicator — if returns disappoint, vendor financing could amplify a funding dry-up. Long-term bear case: capital destruction + market share loss to cheaper Chinese open-source LLMs. 22V separately notes cheap Chinese AI would primarily pressure AI equity valuations rather than slow the broader economy, and that AI capex hasn't driven most US GDP growth due to import leakage. Both flag US 10Y >4.5% as an equity warning signal.

bullets.title: Fed's Waller shifts hawkish; balance of risks moving from labor to inflation
bullets.body: 22V Research highlights that Fed Governor Waller's focus has shifted toward persistent inflation risks, increasing the importance of upcoming CPI data and the Fed reaction function. PSC Macro separately notes June headline CPI is expected to tick down 0.1% m/m to 3.8% y/y on lower energy prices, while NY Fed consumer inflation expectations edged up to 3.7% in June. The dot-plot framework is described as increasingly vulnerable.

bullets.title: Trade deficit cuts 2Q GDP by ~1pp; tariff effective rate collapsed from 11% to <7%
bullets.body: PSC Macro estimates trade will be a net 1 percentage point drag on 2Q GDP after inventory offsets. The tariff effective rate tumbled from 11% to less than 7%, with net tariffs turning negative in June after backing out refunds. MS trade data confirms: May goods exports fell 6.5% m/m in real terms, real capital goods ex-auto imports fell 1% m/m, and 2Q26 GDP tracking is maintained at 2.0% q/q SAAR.

bullets.title: Samsung -9% despite 19x profit growth; memory at 'peak rate of change' near-term
bullets.body: Samsung reported 2Q26 OP of Won 89.4tn (+56% QoQ, +1812% YoY), beating consensus but well below bullish buy-side estimates of ~Won 100tn. Multiple desks flag that memory is approaching a 'peak rate of change' with y/y pricing dynamics and inventory levels historically associated with a stock pause or correction. However, Klein notes Q3 DRAM ASPs could rise 20-30% QoQ per Adata, with structural DDR5 shortages (fulfillment ratio ~70%) supporting a bullish DRAM pricing setup into 2027.

bullets.title: SpaceX gets simultaneous Overweight initiations from MS ($300 PT) and JPM ($225) and Citi ($200/$900+ LT)
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley (PT $300, bull $600), JPMorgan (PT $225), and Citi (PT $200 YE, $900+ LT) all initiated coverage of SpaceX today. MS forecasts revenue scaling from $45B in 2026 to $319B in 2030, driven by Starlink connectivity and orbital AI compute; not FCF-positive before 2035, requiring ~$84B/year in external capital 2027-2034. MS also cuts TMUS PT to $230, T to $25, and CMCSA to $30 as cable broadband subs are modeled to decline ~3-4% CAGR through 2030.

bullets.title: 'Time to power' thesis intact despite last week's selloff; META cloud plans validate compute bottleneck
bullets.body: MS argues Meta's cloud expansion plans confirm that power access remains the gating bottleneck for AI infrastructure, with Meta capex growing from $145bn (2026) to $205bn (2028). Bitcoin-to-datacenter powered shell contracts are pricing at $10-12/watt with 15-19% unlevered FCF yields — value creation per GW ~15x higher than renewable PPAs. Data centers are also migrating to 800VDC architectures, creating opportunities for solid-state transformer and BESS providers.

bullets.title: Jefferies: Software sector down 14%; prefer AI infrastructure over application software
bullets.body: Jefferies cautions that software development costs are falling, AI giants (OpenAI, Anthropic) may capture more supply-chain value, and AI agents could reduce the importance of systems-of-record. Firm prefers AI infrastructure and usage beneficiaries (AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, SNOW, CRWV, ORCL) over traditional application software, with seat-based pricing models viewed as particularly at risk.

bullets.title: Broad market: S&P +0.7% to 7,488; VIX +5.7% to 16.45; semis the main drag
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures were +0.15% early morning and the index is up 0.7% to 7,488 by late morning. The 10-year yield is +2 bps to 4.49%. Semiconductor names are the primary drag: AMD -4.4%, MU -5.1%, STX -6.4%, WDC -7.2% on DeepSeek chip concerns, while NVDA -1.6%. AI software names outperform with NET +5.0%, NOW +3.7%.

bullets.title: HF positioning: most sold June in PB history; $484B in excess selling underwater, short squeeze risk building
bullets.body: UBS notes hedge funds net sold for a third consecutive week; June was the most sold month in prime brokerage book history. Crowded winners are de-grossing at -2.0 standard deviations and high-momentum names are down -7% of total US GMV. Composite manager positioning has moved to <0.5std overweight from ~1.5std, with Risk Control and CTA exposures below longer-term averages. $484bn in excess June selling is now underwater, creating building short-squeeze risk.

bullets.title: Internet sector +6% YTD vs SPX +2%; valuations at 23-25x 2026E EPS, down vs TTM averages
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reports internet names up 6% YTD vs. SPX +2% and NDX +1%. GOOGL and META lead (+7%, +6%), AMZN +4%, with RDDT +17% and APP +10% as standouts. Valuations are compressed vs. trailing averages: AMZN at 25x 2026E EPS (down 26% vs. TTM avg), GOOGL at 25x (down 20%), META at 23x (down 6%). Industry view remains Attractive.

bullets.title: BoJ on track for another hike; 10-year JGB hits 30-year high of 2.85%
bullets.body: Japanese nominal wages grew 3.2% y/y in May with real wages +1.4%, validating BoJ hawks. Markets price an 84% probability of another BoJ rate hike by year-end to 1.25%. The 10-year JGB yield hit a 30-year high of 2.85% today, adding to global duration pressure. The ultra-weak yen remains a tailwind for Nikkei equities.

bullets.title: Macro regime: normal expansion, not risk-off; rotation theme intact with banks/retail as biggest upside
bullets.body: 22V Research argues the current regime is a normal economic expansion with fundamentals driving returns, not multiple expansion. S&P 500 CY26 EPS is expected to grow ~25% with Q2 earnings and sales expected to beat meaningfully. Banks, Retail, Homebuilders, and Transports offer greatest asymmetric upside. Nearby recession odds remain low; Morgan Stanley similarly recommends leaning into large-cap banks on capital markets strength ahead of 2Q earnings.

bullets.title: Bonds weakening; XHB puts flagged as attractive with 31 homebuilders reporting before Aug 21
bullets.body: 22V Research recommends buying XHB August 107 puts at ~$3.25 (reference ~$110), noting XHB rallied ~26% from May lows but appears overvalued relative to bond weakness. TLT failed at its 200-day MA and broke below uptrend support. With at least 31 of 38 XHB constituents reporting earnings before August 21 and put volatility near recent lows, the risk/reward is viewed as compelling.

bullets.title: FSLR upgraded to Buy at Deutsche Bank; utilities with data center exposure highlighted as undervalued
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank upgraded FSLR to Buy with a PT of $272 (from $245), citing stronger second-half fundamentals and S232 policy clarifications. Wells Fargo screens FE and EXC as utilities with data center exposure trading at steep discounts, and Mizuho identifies AEP, DUK, EXC, FE, SRE, SO, and PPL as having the highest data center exposure in a 309-location dataset.

bullets.title: European data center capacity forecasts raised +15% to >40GW; optical market set for ~40% CAGR through 2028
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised European data center capacity forecasts +15% to >40GW, expecting +21% pa growth through 2030. Europe's optical market is forecast to grow at ~40% CAGR through 2028 as AI infrastructure drives a multi-year connectivity bottleneck. NATO and EC targets create ~$390bn cumulative defence demand over 10 years; AI adoption surveys show 5% net job losses over the past 12 months across covered sectors.

bullets.title: Oil: Saudi Arabia cuts Arab Light crude by $11/barrel — largest cut in 26 years
bullets.body: OPCO notes Saudi Arabia cut Arab Light crude pricing by $11/barrel, $1.50 vs. regional benchmarks — the largest cut in 26 years. Energy sector saw $3.2B in outflows last week, the largest in two years. MS European strategy separately lowered its 2027 Dated Brent forecast to $75/bbl in 1H27 and $70/bbl in 2H27, citing physical glut from high US exports and low Chinese imports.

bullets.title: Walmart ignites grocery price war; beef -12%, Coke ~-30%; MS flags race-to-the-bottom margin risk
bullets.body: Walmart is aggressively cutting prices including ground beef -12%, Coke ~30%, and expanding across household, toys, and apparel categories. Morgan Stanley flags a potential race-to-the-bottom in grocery margins. WMT shares rallied on the news; KeyBanc separately continues to favor WMT for ongoing share gains in hardlines/broadlines, raising WSM PT to $250.
